messages.text: Ok, cool - looks like there's new reviwer comments. Follow them up in a new PR - as they will concern the muon chamber layout more than the toroidal magentic system.
I’ll read the new comments on PR #87 and handle the muon chamber layout changes in a separate PR.

The comments request rectangular barrel chambers, trapezoidal endcap chambers, and a frame with feet connecting and supporting the coils. I’ll keep PR #87’s magnetic layout fixed, develop those additions in a new PR, and quantify coverage across the full solid angle, including unavoidable openings.

The chamber shapes have a real packing consequence: flat 500 mm chambers need gaps between modules and space around the coil returns. I’m using whole rectangular and trapezoidal envelopes and will report both measurement-plane crossings and complete depth traversals, so the coverage figures expose those losses.

The support model now connects all 36 coil cases to the frame and feet through finite contact patches. I’m checking the chamber modules against those supports and the fixed coil envelopes, then measuring coverage over the full solid angle.

The finite chamber shapes expose gaps that the ideal shells hid, especially near coil returns and endcap support spokes. I’m keeping only whole modules that pass volume and clearance checks; the coverage maps will show the remaining gaps.

The draft has 1,560 whole chamber modules and a connected frame with ten feet. The first coverage grids showed substantial sampling sensitivity around narrow gaps, so I’m increasing the grid density and adding an independent random-ray integral before reporting coverage percentages.

The independent million-ray integral gives about 63% three-station coverage with the assumed inactive borders, and about 41% when requiring complete chamber-depth traversal. I’m using the repository’s design-evidence and review workflow to document these limits and obtain an independent review before opening the PR.

The frame reduces three-station coverage by about 2.8 percentage points in the paired packing comparison. Its estimated self-mass is about 129.5 tonnes; all 36 coil identities have checked connections to ground. These are space, connectivity and mass checks—magnetic loads and structural strength still need engineering analysis.

The prototype and figures are committed, with all 70 relevant controls passing. I’m getting an independent review of that exact revision, focusing on clearance proofs, station counting and the coverage claims, before opening the separate PR.

I’m opening a separate PR stacked on #87 while the final review runs. It includes rectangular barrel chambers, trapezoidal endcap chambers, and the frame and feet, with the substantial coverage gaps stated explicitly. The magnetic layout and joint field map remain unchanged.

[PR #90](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/90) is open separately from #87. Its new geometry tests and inherited magnetic checks have passed in CI. The token dashboard build is also green; the remaining repository checks and independent review are still running.

The reviewer has reproduced all 21 new controls and checked all four figures, with no blocker found so far. The remaining checks audit the saved chamber geometry and coverage arithmetic against the frozen source revision.

The independent geometry audit found no blocker: it confirmed chamber and support separation, all 1,310 material contacts, ground connectivity, and the coverage arithmetic. I’m retaining that review in the PR, then will mark it ready and link it back to the original review thread.

Created [PR #90](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/90), ready for review and linked from #87.

It adds rectangular barrel and trapezoidal endcap chamber outlines, a connected frame and feet. The magnetic layout/map remain unchanged.

70 targeted controls pass; independent review found no blockers. Coverage gaps are documented. Final CI is running.
